_about:
Phase D-2b scenario metadata.  The d2b-twelve-scenarios.sh bash script
  reads this file INSTEAD of inferring verdict expectations from baked-in branches
  inside the script.  Two reasons:
  (a) chart-policy-driven CLOSED verdicts are graded CHART_INTENTIONAL_DENY
      so PASS_OK math is well-defined and chart-policy regressions are loud
      (they flip CHART_INTENTIONAL_DENY to DENY_LEAK);
  (b) fixture source/target identity, namespaces, etc. are pulled from this
      single file so CNI tests and fixture YAMLs cannot drift.

  d2b.53: `source` and `target` carry EXACT manifest-aligned Pod identity.
  The runner no longer rediscovers fixture Pods through label selectors — the
  historical `app=cni-source` / `app=cni-target` selectors never existed in
  01-test-pods.yaml / 02-stub-deps.yaml, so every scenario silently SKIPped
  and the gate reported a zero-work TOTAL=0 success.  Identity now comes from
  this document and is independently re-validated against Kubernetes JSON
  (exact namespace/name, not deleting, phase=Running, Ready=True, exactly one
  match) before any traffic is requested.

  Each entry has:
    id:            stable scenario id used in the run record
    description:   human-readable summary
    role:          gateway | worker | ingress-controller | prometheus | untrusted
    action:        what the source pod does (http_get, tcp_connect, dns_lookup)
    source:        { namespace, pod_name } — EXACT tracked fixture Pod that
                   originates the L3 request.  Reconciled 1:1 against
                   01-test-pods.yaml.
    target_kind:   service | pod | external_ip
    target:        for target_kind=service:
                     { namespace, pod_name, service_fqdn } — EXACT tracked
                     fixture Pod behind the Service, reconciled 1:1 by
                     resolving the Service selector against the fixture Pod
                     label sets.  L1 execs inside this Pod.
                   for target_kind=external_ip:
                     { kind: external_ip, host, port, l1_l2_exempt: true,
                       namespace: null, pod_name: null } — the literal external
                       address/port is retained and the L1/L2 exemption is
                       explicit.  No target Pod is invented.
    target_svc:    ClusterIP service FQDN (if target_kind=service)
    target_host:   hostname or IP the source connects to
    target_port:   int
    expected:      ALLOW | DENY
    chart_intent:  ALLOW_IMPLIED | ALLOW_FEATURE_OFF | DENY_DEFAULT_DENY | DENY_DIRECT_EGRESS
                    | DENY_PORT_MISUSE | DENY_EXTERNAL_IP | DENY_METADATA | DENY_OPEN_INTENT
    upstream_reason:        short text used for hints when regressed
    requires_features:      list<name> — keys in values.yaml that must be true
    ignores_l1:   bool — true when the target has no localhost listener by definition
    ignores_l2:   bool — true when the host is a raw IP / not a service hostname

  Expected counts are DERIVED from this document (len(scenarios)); the gate
  never hard-codes 12 or 13 even though the historical script filename and the
  workflow step text say "twelve".
